diagnoses.description: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease

claim_lines.description: Office or other outpatient visit for evaluation and management of an established patient, high complexity

medical_record_excerpt: 71-year-old male with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%), type 2 diabetes, and CKD stage 3b presents with 4 days of worsening dyspnea on exertion, 2-pillow orthopnea, and 3 kg weight gain. BP 152/94, HR 104, SpO2 91% on room air. Bilateral 2+ pitting lower-extremity edema and bibasilar crackles. Point-of-care BNP 1240 pg/mL. Assessment: acute on chronic HFrEF exacerbation. Furosemide increased from 40mg daily to 40mg twice daily; potassium and creatinine recheck ordered in 48 hours. Emergency department evaluation recommended; patient declined after risk discussion. Shared decision for close outpatient management with daily weights, strict return precautions, and follow-up visit in 48 hours. Total time on date of service: 52 minutes.

extracted_entities.text: Furosemide 40mg daily increased to 40mg twice daily

policy_sources: AMA CPT 2024 Evaluation and Management Guidelines, Table 2 (MDM Scoring)

line_reviews.rationale: Documentation supports high-complexity MDM: acute exacerbation of chronic illness posing a threat to bodily function, prescription drug management with dose escalation, and a documented decision regarding hospitalization. 52 minutes of total time also documented.
BNP performed and resulted to evaluate suspected heart failure exacerbation.
